questions.q: What did the sons of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun do with harps, lyres, and cymbals?
questions.a: They lead the worship music at the temple with harps, lyres, and cymbals.

questions.q: Who were the sons of Asaph, and who directed them?
questions.a: The sons of Asaph were Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asharelah. Asaph directed them.

questions.q: For what did the sons of Jeduthun play the harp?
questions.a: They played the harp to thank and praise Yahweh.

questions.q: What did God give Heman in order to honor him?
questions.a: God gave him fourteen sons and three daughters.

questions.q: Who directed the musicians, and who supervised their fathers?
questions.a: Their fathers directed them as they played cymbals, harps, and lyres for the service of Yahweh’s house, and the king supervised their fathers Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman.

questions.q: How many men were trained and skilled in the songs of Yahweh?
questions.a: There were 288 men who were trained and skilled in the songs of Yahweh.

questions.q: Which of the musicians were included when they cast lots for their duties?
questions.a: All of the musicians cast lots for their duties, both those with more experience and those with less experience, the teacher as well as the student.

questions.q: How were the twenty-four groups of musicians assigned their order of service, and how many men were in each group?
questions.a: They cast lots to determine the order, from the first lot for Joseph to the twenty-fourth lot for Romamti Ezer, and each lot selected a group of 12 men.

commentary.text: —David put those in order who were appointed to be singers and musicians in the temple. To prophesy, in this place, means praising God with great earnestness and devout affections, under the influences of the Holy Spirit. In raising these affections, poetry and music were employed. If the Spirit of God do not put life and fervour into our devotions, they will, however ordered, be a lifeless, worthless form.
